advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'measured zero Bedrock token metrics' from 'no metric series were found at all' in _metered_spend and log/alert loudly on the latter.
evidence: `total = 0.0` initialised and returned unchanged when no metric matches
`if len(dims) != 1 or dims[0]["Name"] != "ModelId": continue` silently drops any series that does not match the expected shape
ABSENCE: no assertion/log that list_metrics returned at least one AWS/Bedrock token series before trusting total==0 as 'no spend'
`_metered_spend` contains no try/except while _refresh_rates, CE poll, _apply and _notify are all individually guarded
`metered = _metered_spend(day_start, now, rates)` at handler.py:418 is called with no surrounding guard
advisory.finding: The CloudWatch metered signal fails open: if list_metrics returns no matching per-ModelId series (wrong region, throttling, metrics not yet emitted, or a namespace/dimension shape change), _metered_spend returns 0.0, which is indistinguishable from 'measured and spend is genuinely zero'. The fast tripwire then silently contributes nothing and enforcement degrades to the 8-24h-lagged CE signal without any signal that the fast path produced no data.
merged_from: A CloudWatch API failure (list_metrics/get_metric_data) inside _metered_spend is uncaught and there is no per-region try/except, so a transient error in one region aborts the entire tick before enforcement runs — and unlike CE/rate refresh/SNS, this path has no fallback or notification.
scenarios: Bedrock emits metrics under a changed dimension/namespace and every series is skipped, so metered=0 while real spend accrues
A region in REGIONS throttles list_metrics returning empty pages
advisory.suggested_fix: Track whether any matching per-ModelId series was seen; if none were found across all REGIONS while CE shows non-trivial spend, log a warning and consider it a degraded state rather than a clean zero.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not set tripped_day when DRY_RUN suppressed the actual attach, or key tripped_day off whether _apply actually touched principals.
evidence: `if DRY_RUN: ... return touched` in _apply returns without attaching (handler.py ~ _apply)
`touched = _apply(attach=True)` followed by `state["tripped_day"] = day.isoformat()` unconditionally on the trip branch
release branch guarded by `state.get("tripped_day") != day.isoformat()`
advisory.finding: On the trip path tripped_day is set even when DRY_RUN=true (because _apply returns early without attaching but tripped_day is still written). After DRY_RUN is later cleared within the same UTC day, the release branch's guard `state.get("tripped_day") != day.isoformat()` is now false, so the cap can neither be shown as tripped (nothing attached) nor auto-released that day.
scenarios: Operator sets DRY_RUN=true to lift the cap for the day (as the README suggests), a dry-run tick records tripped_day, operator reverts DRY_RUN — same-day release logic is now confused
advisory.suggested_fix: Only set state['tripped_day'] when not DRY_RUN (or when touched is non-empty).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make same-day release robust to lost/empty state so a mid-day release cannot occur when tripped_day is unknown.
evidence: `elif attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and state.get("tripped_day") != day.isoformat():`
_load_state returns {} on corrupt/unreadable state (handler.py:_load_state), so tripped_day is lost
README: 'The Lambda will not re-attach within the same UTC day once tripped_day is set'
advisory.finding: The auto-release branch only fires when the deny is attached AND tripped_day != today. If the deny becomes attached without tripped_day being set for today (e.g. state parameter was reset/corrupted and returned empty, or attach happened via a run whose _save_state failed), the same-day release logic will still work next day — but a deny attached with no recorded tripped_day and spend under threshold on the SAME day will be released immediately, contradicting the 'stays tripped for the rest of the UTC day' contract in the README.
scenarios: State parameter is reset or a put_parameter failed after a trip; next tick sees attached=True, tripped_day absent, spend momentarily under cap and detaches mid-day

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard CE Amount extraction with .get chains / broaden the except so a malformed CE response falls back to cached spend instead of crashing.
evidence: `return float(results[0]["Total"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"])` assumes keys exist
CE poll caller only catches ClientError: `except ClientError as exc:` at handler.py:436
KeyError is not a ClientError and would propagate
advisory.finding: _ce_spend_today and _refresh_rates read UnblendedCost/UsageQuantity Amount fields without guarding against absent keys; a Cost Explorer response shape without 'Total'/'UnblendedCost' for a period (possible for a day with no records) can raise KeyError rather than the handled ClientError, crashing the tick uncaught.
scenarios: CE returns a ResultsByTime entry lacking a Total/UnblendedCost block for a metric-less day

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the watched REGIONS list from Terraform variables rather than hardcoding, or document that region is fixed to us-east-1/us-west-2 regardless of var.aws_region.
evidence: `REGIONS = "us-east-1,us-west-2"` hardcoded in the tf environment block
`ce = boto3.client("ce", region_name="us-east-1")` hardcoded in handler.py
policy ARNs templated on `${var.aws_region}` (bedrock_spend_cap.tf:278,295)
advisory.finding: The IAM Logs statement Resource uses `${var.aws_region}` but the CE client is pinned to us-east-1 and CloudWatch is queried in us-east-1,us-west-2; if var.aws_region is ever changed from its us-east-1 default, the SSM state-parameter ARN and log-group ARN in the policy follow var.aws_region while the Lambda runtime region also follows it — but REGIONS and the CE endpoint are hardcoded, creating a silent coupling where a non-default region deploy watches the wrong regions.
scenarios: Someone overrides var.aws_region; the Lambda's monitored REGIONS no longer relate to the deployment region

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CloudWatch alarm on the bedrock-spend-cap Lambda Errors/Invocations (and a DLQ or on-failure destination) so silent enforcement failure is alerted.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:345 `resource "aws_lambda_function" "bedrock_spend_cap" {` — no `dead_letter_config`, no on-failure destination, and no companion `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` on the function's Errors metric
README: 'a timeout here means the cap silently stops being enforced' (handler timeout comment mirrors this)
Repo baseline: monitoring.tf defines aws_sns_topic.alerts + many aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resources wired to alarm_actions, a pattern not applied to this safety-critical Lambda
ABSENCE: search for `bedrock_spend_cap` across infra/terraform returns no aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resource
advisory.finding: The enforcement Lambda (aws_lambda_function.bedrock_spend_cap) has no CloudWatch alarm on its Errors/Invocations metrics and no dead-letter/on-failure destination, so a persistently failing or timing-out function silently stops enforcing the spend cap with no notification — a gap the handler and README both explicitly acknowledge.
scenarios: Lambda throws every tick (e.g. CE/CloudWatch throttling, code regression) and the cap silently never trips
Cold-start paging of all AWS/Bedrock metrics in two regions exceeds the 120s timeout during a real runaway

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a dead_letter_config/retry_policy to the EventBridge target so dropped enforcement ticks are captured and visible.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:414 `resource "aws_cloudwatch_event_target" "bedrock_spend_cap_tick" {` — only rule/target_id/arn set; no `dead_letter_config` or `retry_policy` block
advisory.finding: The EventBridge target (aws_cloudwatch_event_target.bedrock_spend_cap_tick) declares no dead_letter_config or retry_policy, so a dropped/failed invocation of the 5-minute tick is lost with no visibility.
scenarios: EventBridge fails to deliver a tick (throttling, transient Lambda unavailability) and the invocation is silently dropped

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound/trim the rates persisted to SSM (or use Advanced tier / a separate store) so state stays under the 4096-char String parameter limit.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:104 `ssm.put_parameter(Name=STATE_PARAM, Value=json.dumps(state), Type="String", Overwrite=True)`
handler stores `state["rates"] = rates` (the full derived rate table) into that same parameter

infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf State Sid grants only `ssm:GetParameter`/`ssm:PutParameter` on `parameter/${local.bedrock_cap_name}/state` — a standard-tier String parameter with a 4096-char limit
advisory.finding: The handler persists the full empirical `rates` dict into a single SSM parameter created as Type="String", which is capped at 4096 characters; as the per-usage-type rate table grows across regions and models, ssm.put_parameter can begin failing (ValidationException) and wedge state writes.
scenarios: A 60-day rate window across us-east-1+us-west-2 accumulates enough USAGE_TYPE keys that the serialized state exceeds 4096 bytes and put_parameter raises ValidationException

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add table-driven unit tests for _rate_for covering exact-match, seed, observed-input×multiplier, and fail-closed fallback, including substring-collision inputs.
evidence: handler.py:242  `if norm == target or norm in target or target in norm:`
handler.py:256-262  base fallback then `return UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K * mult`
Docstring lines 213-221 declare the 4-step resolution order and the fail-closed guarantee, but search of tests/ for 'bedrock_spend_cap' returned '(no matches)' — the ladder is verified nowhere.
advisory.finding: _rate_for's fail-closed contract is untested: for an unpriced model with empty rates and no seed the function must return UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K * mult, but the substring match `norm == target or norm in target or target in norm` can silently cross-match a different model's usage-type and price the runaway at the wrong (possibly cheaper) rate, defeating the cap's fail-closed guarantee. Named violating input: _rate_for('mistral.large-2', 'OutputTokenCount', {'USE1-mistral.large-input-tokens': 0.001}) — 'mistrallarge' is a substring of the target 'mistrallarge2' (or vice versa) so an input-only observed rate for a different variant is scaled ×5 and returned instead of the intended per-variant rate. No test exercises any branch of this resolution ladder.
scenarios: A new/renamed model whose id substring-collides with an existing billed usage type is priced at the wrong observed rate instead of failing closed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit tests for _rate_for and _normalise asserting each rung of the resolution ladder and the UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K*mult fallback for an unmatched model.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for _seed_for across all four TOKEN_METRICS metrics and for seeds missing 'input' or 'output'.
evidence: handler.py:200-209 cache-read/write multipliers and the `base is None` early return
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:96-100 seeds claude-haiku/sonnet/opus input+output only (no cache fields)
No test references _seed_for (search of tests/ for the module: '(no matches)').
advisory.finding: _seed_for's OutputTokenCount / missing-input behavior is untested. For a seed dict that has only 'input' and metric 'OutputTokenCount', _seed_for returns prices.get('output') == None, dropping to the observed-input×5 or fail-closed path; for a seed with only 'output' and metric 'InputTokenCount', base is None so it returns None. These branch outcomes determine whether the Claude seed rates actually protect a first-ever run, and none is asserted. Named violating input: _seed_for('claude-opus', 'CacheReadInputTokenCount', ...) must return input*0.10 = 0.00055 given SEED_RATES claude-opus input=0.0055 — untested.
scenarios: A first-ever Claude cache-read/write invocation before any bill exists relies entirely on these derived seed multipliers.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add handler() unit tests (boto3 clients mocked at the AWS boundary) asserting attach on trip, no same-day release when tripped_day==today, and release on a new UTC day under cap.
evidence: handler.py:447 trip branch `if spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached:`
handler.py:460 release branch `elif attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and state.get('tripped_day') != day.isoformat():`
No test drives handler() (search of tests/ and repo for the module returned no test references).
blocking.finding: The handler trip/release state machine is untested. The release branch is gated on `attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and state.get('tripped_day') != day.isoformat()`, meaning a cap tripped and set tripped_day=today will NOT auto-release the same UTC day even if spend later reads below threshold — a subtle, intentional behavior with no regression test. Named violating scenario: state={'tripped_day': today}, attached=True, spend below threshold → handler must NOT call _apply(attach=False); the complementary new-day scenario (tripped_day=yesterday) must release. Neither is asserted.
scenarios: Same-day flap: cap trips, spend estimate dips below threshold within the same UTC day.
New UTC day rollover with spend back under cap (auto-release).
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test module invoking handler with monkeypatched iam/ssm/ce/cloudwatch/sns clients and asserting the _apply(attach=...) calls and returned effective_usd/deny_attached for each state.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test module for handler.py (pure functions + handler() with AWS clients mocked at the boundary) and ensure CI runs it.
evidence: search_files tests/ 'bedrock_spend_cap' -> '(no matches)'
repo-wide search 'bedrock-spend-cap' -> only bedrock_spend_cap.tf and README.md hits
terraform-drift.yml:119-144 runs only `terraform plan` (fmt/validate/plan); no pytest step touches handler.py
blocking.finding: The new module ships with no test file and no CI harness executes it. handler.py is entirely added lines, but the only workflow covering infra/terraform (terraform-drift.yml) runs terraform fmt/validate/plan and never pytest, so none of the Python enforcement logic is exercised by CI. This is a whole-module regression-coverage gap for newly introduced behavior.
scenarios: Any future edit to pricing, normalisation, or the state machine merges with no automated behavioral check.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make cap enforcement reconcile the FULL target set each tick (attach to every principal missing the deny) instead of short-circuiting on the first attached target, so a partial attach failure self-heals.
evidence: handler.py:356-386 `_apply` catches ClientError per principal and only logs: `except ClientError as exc: log.error("failed to %s role %s: %s", ...)` — a failed attach does not abort or re-signal
handler.py:335-353 `_is_attached` returns True on the first target with the deny: `if any(p["PolicyArn"] == DENY_POLICY_ARN ...): return True`
handler.py:447 trip guard `if spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached:` — once attached==True (one success), the branch is skipped and unattached targets are never re-attempted
ABSENCE: no reconciliation loop compares the set of principals actually carrying the deny against the full TARGET_ROLES/TARGET_GROUPS set
blocking.finding: Partial attach failure leaves a permanent hole in the cap for the rest of the UTC day: _apply() swallows per-principal ClientError (best-effort) and _is_attached() returns True as soon as ANY single target carries the deny. Once one attach succeeds and tripped_day is set, the trip branch guard `spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached` evaluates False on every subsequent tick, so principals whose attach FAILED are never retried and keep invoking Bedrock uncapped until 00:00 UTC.
scenarios: Cap trips; iam.attach_role_policy succeeds for lmn-api but throttles/errors for lmn-doc-extractor and the Admin group; those principals continue spending on Bedrock for the remainder of the day while the cap reports 'tripped'
blocking.suggested_fix: Have _is_attached (or a new helper) return the set of principals still MISSING the deny, and in the trip branch attach to that missing set on every tick while spend>=THRESHOLD, rather than gating on a single-target boolean.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Track per-principal attach/detach outcomes and drive both trip and release toward full convergence, verifying every target reaches the intended state before recording tripped/released.
evidence: handler.py:460 `elif attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and state.get("tripped_day") != day.isoformat():`
handler.py:372-386 detach path swallows ClientError per group/role without recording which principals remain denied
ABSENCE: no post-detach verification that every target is free of DENY_POLICY_ARN
dropped.finding: The release branch is guarded by `attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and state.get('tripped_day') != day`, but a partial detach failure is not tracked: if _apply(attach=False) fails for some principals (ClientError swallowed), _is_attached() may still return True (another principal still denied) and the branch will re-run detach on the already-detached ones while the failed ones are only retried opportunistically — there is no explicit convergence check that ALL targets are detached before considering the cap released.
scenarios: New UTC day, spend under cap, detach succeeds for roles but errors for the Admin group; Admin remains denied Bedrock invocation while the run reports 'released', potentially blocking legitimate production Bedrock use until a later tick happens to succeed
